en: The *Vajraguhyasudvāradhāraṇī-mantra-sūtra*, translator unknown;
now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was at the Auspicious Site of Enlightenment (*Mūlaguṇa-maṇḍala*) beneath the Bodhi tree, and he addressed [the assembly]:
The bhikṣus, the Venerable Śāriputra, the Venerable Ānanda,
and such other assemblies of śrāvakas, as well as the great bodhisattvas,
whose names were as follows: the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja.
With Vajragarbha Bodhisattva and Maitreya Bodhisattva as their leaders, there were all such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of this Bhadrakalpa.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
we only pray that the World-Honored One will preach the *Śubhamukha-dhāraṇī*,
so as to provide illumination for all sentient beings.
They shall not be afflicted or harmed by any evils—
whether by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
kumbhāṇḍas, or humans and non-humans.
If there are those who rob others of their vital essence—
whether by means of weapons, staffs, poisons, incantations, or insect-inflicted treatments;
whether while eating, drinking, walking, lying down, sleeping, or dreaming.
If enemies are engaged in strife and mutual verbal contention,
by reciting this dhāraṇī,
none of their evils shall be able to cause harm. At that time, the Buddha praised the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada! Listen well now;
I shall explain for you the *Sugata-mukha-dhāraṇī*.
Those who wish to seek the protection and deliverance of all sentient beings [should hear it].
Then he spoke the mantra:
*tadyathā | oṃ kumāru kumāru | māpini | mandani mandani | vara | carini hū hū | lohita svāhā*. This is protected and sustained by the consecration phrases of all the Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Buddha again repeated this mantra:
*tadyathā hoṅgi hoṅgi hoṅgira-dari*.
Ho-gi-ra ho-te-ho-gi-ra pi-te-ho-gi-ra da-ti.
Cakrāho-giri-cakrādali dali dali trili.
Cale kṣu kṣudraka speye lili lili śiri śiri lulu zhi.
Cāre cūḍe maute maṃtale sarvabhāṣye naye.
Cīcī dūvili māli hatani pāri.
Vāribhadri, Vibhidi, Vāriyāśari.
Śaraviro haniro haṇata che saha macchaliṇa.

Namo indrāya, devendrāya, mahendra-rājñe. Namo maheśvarāya, rājñe. Namo mārīcaye. Namo brahmaṇe. Namo brahmendrāya. Namo brahmarājñe. Namo bhagavate. Namo buddhāya. Namo dharmāya. Namo saṃghāya. Namo śākyamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Namo vajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Namo āryamahāsthāmaprāptāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryasamantabhadrāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryamaitreyāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatīśvarībodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarībodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo āryavajrārciṣmatītejovatīśvarīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñīrājñyai bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Namo
The Master said:
"Bambuni, pāpāñjanī, kara-avaṭe, puṭa-avaṭe."
Svāhā somavati te somaprabhe svāhā.
Cīrṇe yoge ātāyate dhite hāre hāre hāre khele idammodapūche.
Bhagavān āha tadyathā.
Khaṭṭa vatta ajita alinda nika gaddani aratāhani.
Makā-vilohani-hūṣavate-buṣavate-hiri-hiriyā-ta-śe.
Jaya ajine jaya pāliñche jaya vāniye.
Yetha khiladāyana vasiṭhṭhaputta.

Sumukha-tāraṇi-patani | Tathāgatena vasi-ta-sarvasattva-namatthaya | Karuṇātaye ahaṃ-paśami | Yatthate vipākī | Tathāgata-arhat-samyak-saṃbodhi-vasita | Aticchita | Sarvajña-bodhir-naspi-vatā-pitā | Then the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi.
I wish to benefit all sentient beings by proclaiming this dhāraṇī.
Just as the Buddhas of the past received, upheld, and protected it,
I too shall protect and uphold it.
At that time, the Buddha emitted light from the ūrṇā-kośa on the crown of his head,
manifesting the marks of a Great Man that shone throughout the ten directions,
pervading all the worlds of the Buddhas without exception.
The Buddhas each spoke with one voice in praise, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Buddha!
You have skillfully expounded this *śubhamukha-dhāraṇī*."
They act as a light for all sentient beings;
we, too, shall uphold and protect them, exclaiming, "Excellent! Excellent!"
Furthermore, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this *Śubhamukha Dhāraṇī*,
all Buddhas shall constantly protect and mind them throughout the morning.
Any previously committed karmic retributions and obstacles shall gradually be eliminated.
These good sons further obtain twenty kinds of merit:
first, long life; second, longevity.
Third is renown;
fourth is being heard of afar;
fifth is great wealth.
Sixth is great strength;
seventh is physical comeliness;
eighth is a fine complexion.
Ninth, the primary and secondary marks;
tenth, the adornment of the body;
eleventh, freedom from illness.
Twelfth is peace and happiness;
thirteenth is being protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas;
fourteenth is being guarded by all devas.
Fifteenth is the maturation of the roots of goodness;
sixteenth is diligence;
seventeenth is tirelessness.
Eighteenth is eloquence;
nineteenth is analytical understanding;
twentieth is the perfection of the roots of goodness.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
they shall obtain the twenty kinds of complete merits as described above.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi:
These dhāraṇīs are all the secret treasury teachings of the Buddhas.
You should receive and uphold them well, ensuring they are not lost or forgotten;
they are the dwelling places of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, I too shall proclaim a dhāraṇī to protect those who receive,
uphold, read, and recite this 'Dhāraṇī of the Gate of Goodness'."
He shall not allow any evils to find an opportunity.
Then he spoke this mantra:

*Śvadi-dhāntam | Śikṣi śikṣi | Ji ji ji ji | Bho bho | Lū lū | Lū lū jhe jhe jhe jhe ga ga ga ga ti ti ti ti | Pha pha pha pha | Ma ma ma ma | Hana hana hana hana | Dha ha dha ha paca pa paca | Svāhā.* At that time, the Buddha again praised the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada.
Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
May your incantations all be divinely efficacious for the benefit of sentient beings.
Should there be anyone who robs others of their spirit, vitality, or breath, [may they be subdued].
"Act as a protector so that they find no opportunity.
At that time, Brahmā Śikhin rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha,
saying, "World-Honored One..."
Furthermore, if there is anyone who receives, maintains, reads, and recites this Śubhamukha Dhāraṇī,
I shall likewise rejoice and proclaim this dhāraṇī to protect that person,
causing all their incantations to attain divine efficacy.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | tiri miri ciri svāhā | bho bho māphuli svāhā | bho bho māspi svāhā | para kāpi-vaḥ pāśaṃ tiri svāhā.* At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra...
Rising from his seat, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall proclaim a dhāraṇī to protect this person;
by receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting it, all evils shall be prevented from finding an opportunity."
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

*Śvete dhāraṇi ho raṇi | hotamale ti ti ti kauri | gandhāri | pramale va | anamaśantadhāraṇi | dhāramalini | cakrāho ki | jambhali jambhali | svāhā.* At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings rose from their seats.
They addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
we four kings shall also recite this dhāraṇī to protect these people,
so that no evils may take advantage of them."
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | bheṣu bheṣu | dumapāri | hiri hiri | yavālasvati | nemudati | maṅgaliduti | dudi svāhā.* At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha...
Extending his right arm, he rubbed the crowns of the heads of Śakra, Brahmā, the World Protectors, and all the manifested beings, and praised them, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You have well expounded this dhāraṇī for the protection of sentient beings."
They shall always be protected and sustained by all the Buddhas.
At that time, the Buddha again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"If there are good men or good women..."
Those who receive, uphold, read, and recite the Shanmen Dhāraṇī shall,
at dawn, be constantly followed,
protected, and assisted by all the Buddhas and all the celestial deities.
Those who sought his faults were unable to find an opportunity.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva,
along with the entire great assembly of devas, humans, gandharvas, asuras, and others—
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
This *Vajraguhya-sudvāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra* differs from the edition in the Dan (Tang) canon.
